1.title: Cloud Security Concepts
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Cloud Security Concepts. It covers the exam area four. Networking and Cloud Security Concepts. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. four point three Understand cloud security: Characteristics (for example broad network access, rapid elasticity, measured service, on-demand self-service, resource pooling). Service models. Deployment models. Shared security model (for example roles and responsibilities). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: four. Networking and Cloud Security Concepts (twenty-one point three percent). Exam format: an adaptive exam of one hundred to one hundred twenty-five questions in two hours; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official I S C two C C exam outline.

1.title: Cloud characteristics
1.text: Cloud characteristics. Cloud computing delivers computing resources as a service over the network, paid by use. The five essential characteristics are. On-demand self-service. The customer provisions resources alone, without a human at the provider. Broad network access. Resources are reached over the network from many kinds of devices. Resource pooling. The provider shares resources among many customers (multi-tenancy). Rapid elasticity. Resources scale up and down quickly to match demand. Measured service. Usage is metered, so you pay for what you use. Exam tip: Self-service, broad network access, pooling, elasticity, measured service. Pooling means many tenants on shared hardware, so isolation matters.

1.title: Service models
1.text: Service models. The figure shows this: Service models: what the customer manages in I A A S, pass and sass.

1.title: Service models, continued
1.text: Service models. Infrastructure as a Service. Provider delivers: Virtual machines, storage, networks. Customer manages: Operating system, applications, data. Example: A virtual server. Platform as a Service. Provider delivers: A platform to build and run apps. Customer manages: Applications and data. Example: A managed database or app platform. Software as a Service. Provider delivers: A finished application. Customer manages: Data, users and settings. Example: Web email, office suites.

1.title: Deployment models
1.text: Deployment models. Public cloud. Who uses it: Many customers share the provider's infrastructure. Note: Cheapest, most elastic; less control. Private cloud. Who uses it: One organization. Note: More control, higher cost. Hybrid cloud. Who uses it: Public and private connected. Note: Flexibility; integration is harder. Community cloud. Who uses it: Several organizations with shared needs (for example agencies). Note: Shared cost and rules.

1.title: The shared responsibility model
1.text: The shared responsibility model. The provider secures the cloud; the customer secures what they put in the cloud. The more the provider manages, the less the customer must do, but data and access are always the customer's. Physical data center, hardware. I A A S: Provider. pass: Provider. sass: Provider. Operating system and patches. I A A S: Customer. pass: Provider. sass: Provider. Applications. I A A S: Customer. pass: Customer. sass: Provider. Data, identities and access. I A A S: Customer. pass: Customer. sass: Customer. Always the customer: data classification, user accounts, access control and configuration. Most cloud breaches come from customer misconfiguration, such as public storage or weak access.

1.title: The shared responsibility model, continued
1.text: The shared responsibility model. When hosting A I in the cloud, the same model applies: the customer protects training data, models and access. Exam tip: Data and identities are always the customer's responsibility, in every model. I A A S gives the most customer responsibility; sass the least. Exam tip: Public, private, hybrid, community describe who shares the cloud. I A A S, pass, sass describe what the provider delivers. Do not mix the two lists.

1.title: Other cloud security points
1.text: Other cloud security points. Data location. Laws may restrict where data is stored (data residency). Service level agreement. The contract for availability and support. Vendor lock-in. Hard to move away from a provider. Shadow I T. Staff using cloud services without approval. Due diligence. Review the provider's audits before choosing.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A customer can create a virtual server at any time from a web portal without contacting the provider. Which characteristic is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: On-demand self-service, which needs no staff help. Provisioning resources alone, without provider staff, is on-demand self-service.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A web shop's capacity grows automatically during a sale and shrinks afterwards. Which characteristic is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Rapid elasticity, which scales with demand. Quickly scaling resources up and down is rapid elasticity.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A company uses a web-based email service and manages only its users and data. Which service model is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Software as a Service. A finished application delivered over the web, with the customer managing users and data, is sass.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. In an I A A S deployment, who is responsible for patching the guest operating system? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The customer, who manages the operating system. In I A A S the customer manages the operating system and above, including patching.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which responsibility belongs to the customer in every cloud service model? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Protection of its own data and user access. Data, identities and access always remain the customer's responsibility.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A company connects its own data center to a public cloud and moves workloads between them. Which deployment model is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Hybrid cloud. A connected mix of private and public resources is a hybrid cloud.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Name the five cloud characteristics. Answer: On-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service. Question two. Who manages the operating system in pass? Answer: The provider. Question three. What is multi-tenancy? Answer: Many customers sharing the same pooled resources.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does the customer always secure? Answer: Its data, identities and access. Question five. What is a hybrid cloud? Answer: Public and private clouds connected together. Question six. What is shadow I T? Answer: Staff using cloud services without approval.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Characteristics: self-service, broad access, pooling, elasticity, measured service. Service models: I A A S (O S and up is yours), pass (apps and data), sass (data and access). Deployment: public, private, hybrid, community. Shared responsibility: provider secures the cloud; customer secures data, identities, configuration.
